cards.text: Job, the man who lost so much (Job 1:13-19), is still talking, right where he left off with his friends. And now he goes somewhere NOBODY saw coming: underground. 'Surely there is a mine for silver and a place where gold is refined.'

cards.question: Silver has its mine, and gold has its place to be refined. Iron, Job says, is taken from the ___.

cards.text: Then Job turns to the miner, who digs for ore in the deepest darkness. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer begging for a little light, and this man goes down there ON PURPOSE.

cards.question: True or false: Job says the darkness deep down in the mine is too much for the miner.
The miner needs a place to cut his shaft. Where does Job say he cuts it?

cards.text: Job says, 'Far from men he dangles and sways.' That's me hanging off the top shelf of my bakery by my mustache, gold base swinging, reaching for the sprinkles.
Then Job points out something wild about the ground. Up top, the earth gives food, but down below it's transformed as by fire.

cards.question: Down in the rocks under the earth, what does Job say is waiting for the miner?

cards.text: No bird of prey knows the path down to that treasure, Job says, and no falcon's eye has seen it.

cards.question: No falcon has seen the miner's path. What does Job say about the proud beasts, like the lion?

answers.text: They've never set foot on it
They hunt along it at night
They guard the way down to it

cards.text: Meanwhile, the miner is going to WORK. He strikes the flint and overturns mountains at their base, and friend, I can't flip one cookie without breaking it.

cards.question: The miner hews out channels in the rocks. True or false: Job says the miner's eyes spot every treasure down there.

cards.text: He even stops up the sources of the streams. WHOLE STREAMS, friend!

cards.question: The miner stops up the streams so he can bring what is hidden to ___.
From silver mines to dark shafts to stopped-up streams, what is Job showing about people?

answers.text: They'll go to great lengths for hidden treasure
They're too afraid to dig deep into the earth
They leave the earth's treasure where it lies

cards.text: Then Job flips the whole thing around. People can dig silver, gold and sapphires out of the dark, 'But where can wisdom be found, and where does understanding dwell?'

cards.question: After all that talk of treasure, Job says no man can know wisdom's ___.
True or false: Job says wisdom can be found in the land of the living.

cards.text: Ask the deep about wisdom, and the ocean depths say, 'It is not in me,' while the sea declares, 'It is not with me.' The sea is the junk drawer of the whole world: EVERYTHING ends up down there, and even IT says nope.

cards.question: Wisdom can't be found down deep. True or false: Job says it can be bought with gold.

cards.text: Then Job lines up the finest treasures on earth next to wisdom: gold of Ophir, onyx, sapphire, crystal, coral, quartz, rubies and topaz from Cush.

cards.question: Gold of Ophir, onyx, sapphire, rubies, topaz from Cush and more. How does Job say all those treasures measure up next to wisdom?

answers.text: None of them can compare to it
Rubies come the closest to it
Together they can match its price

cards.text: So Job asks again where wisdom comes from. It's hidden from the eyes of every living thing, even the birds of the air.

cards.question: Even Abaddon, the place of destruction, and Death speak up about wisdom. What do they say?

answers.text: They've heard a rumor about it

cards.question: Wisdom is hidden from every living thing. Then Job says, 'But God ___ its way, and He knows its place.'
Job says God knows where wisdom is. What reason does Job give?

answers.text: He sees everything under the heavens
The ocean told Him where it was
He dug it up from the mountains

cards.text: Job takes it back to when God fixed the weight of the wind and measured out the waters. He set a limit for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt.

cards.question: Back when God set up the wind and the rain, what did He do with wisdom?

answers.text: He looked at it and established it
He buried it under the deep sea
He handed it to the birds of the air

cards.text: And then God speaks to man and tells him what wisdom is.

cards.question: What does God tell man that wisdom is?
True or false: God tells man that to turn away from evil is understanding.

cards.text: Job's not done talking yet, friend. Keep your apron on, because there's more coming.
